decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 11-0.

changes.quote: Progress on vaccinations has reduced the spread of COVID-19 in the United States.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Amid this progress and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have strengthened.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Amid progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have strengthened.”

changes.quote: The COVID-19 pandemic is causing tremendous human and economic hardship across the United States and around the world.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: The path of the economy will depend significantly on the course of the virus.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The path of the economy will depend significantly on the course of the virus, including progress on vaccinations.”

changes.quote: Progress on vaccinations will likely continue to reduce the effects of the public health crisis on the economy, but risks to the economic outlook remain.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The ongoing public health crisis continues to weigh on the economy, and risks to the economic outlook remain.”

changes.quote: With inflation having run persistently below this longer-run goal, the Committee will aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time so that inflation averages 2 percent over time and longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored at 2 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “With inflation running persistently below this longer-run goal, the Committee will aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time so that inf…”

tone_quotes.quote: These asset purchases help foster smooth market functioning and accommodative financial conditions, thereby supporting the flow of credit to households and businesses.
Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses.

The Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 14.75% APR costs about $61.46 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.57% and moved +6 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 2.99% would rise by about $9.72 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5.8%, and employers added an average of 562k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 4.9% over the past year (May 2021); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 3.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 6.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +5 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.54%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.21% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 90%, cut 5%, hike 5%.
